best_for: Family historians, from weekend hobbyists to professional genealogists, who want their research in a free program on their own computer rather than on a subscription website.

points.title: Built for serious research
points.text: Gramps records people, places and events and the links between them, with as much detail and sourcing as you want. The project aims to be easy for hobbyists and complete enough for professionals.

points.title: Free, open source, offline
points.text: Gramps is free under the GPL 2.0 and has no account or subscription. Your family tree lives on your computer, not on a genealogy site.

points.title: Add-ons extend it, unofficially
points.text: Users and developers write add-ons such as Family Sheet, Graph View and Network Chart. They are not part of Gramps itself, and some need extra libraries, so quality and support vary.

points.title: Back up before you upgrade
points.text: The 6.0.8 release notes advise a backup before upgrading. That habit costs a minute and protects years of research if a new version or add-on misbehaves.

points.title: Installers for every desktop
points.text: Windows gets a 64-bit all-in-one installer, in per-user and all-users forms. Macs get separate disk images for Intel and Apple silicon. A Snap is also published.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is official
points.text: The Flatpak for x64 and Arm64 is published by the Gramps team and verified on Flathub. It is about 71 MiB to download.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 12 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
